decisions.summary: An ejected change or a carry conflict becomes a repair entry in the queue that a fresh builder takes, not an agent the lane launches.
decisions.why: The GM-approved sketch item 1 says it outright: 'the ejected task returns to the queue as a repair entry'. Item 3 has the coordinator as the dispatcher ('I'd dispatch'), and a builder the coordinator dispatches for the entry is a fresh agent that is neither standing nor the coordinator. The coordinator's context gets one queue line. Nothing asked for is narrowed.

decisions.id: XVI-a / D9 + Risks (judgment wakes with no fresh agent)
decisions.summary: Besides repair entries, the lane wakes the coordinator for a set red twice / arbiter owed (D6 step 4), the push failing twice after a re-run (Risks), and the runner dying (D9). The plan does not say who does the integration work after the wake.
decisions.why: Sketch item 3: 'The only integration work left to me would be the rare case that needs judgment, and there a fresh agent per batch beats me doing it'; the plan's own quote of US5 is 'never a standing integrator, never the coordinator's context'. D7 is presented as the plan's answer to US5, but it covers only ejected changes and carry conflicts. A batch that is green but cannot push twice, and a set the arbiter is asked about, wake the coordinator, and the plan names no fresh agent for that batch, which by default leaves the work in the coordinator's turns. That is exactly the case the GM gave to a fresh agent. No impossibility is claimed and none exists, since D7's repair entry could carry them. (A dead runner needs only `make lane-start`, which is a dispatch, not integration, and is fine.)

decisions.summary: Inside the lane, the red-gate tripwire does not fire on consecutive reds that are steps of one halving.
decisions.why: Applied literally, the tripwire would stop the lane at the second step of any bisection. That defeats the GM-approved sketch item 1 ('On a red result it bisects and ejects the failing change') and FR-004, and the plan says so concretely. Exempting a halving's own steps is legitimate.

decisions.id: XVI-b / D6 step 4, part 2 (everything else the set key exempts)
decisions.summary: The exemption is implemented by keying the tripwire to 'a second red of the SAME sorted set of short shas'. That exempts every lane red, not only a halving's steps.
decisions.why: Judged by its purpose, the key leaves the tripwire unable to fire. Every path the plan names gives a fresh set. Halving runs strictly smaller subsets. After an attributed ejection 'the rest runs again' as a new set. The last survivor is 'ejected without a run of its own'. A repair's hand-in supersedes with a NEW sha (D7, D14), so a task that goes red, is repaired, and goes red again never matches. The Risks re-run follows a GREEN gate, so it can give at most one red. Phase 2 states the result itself: the tripwire by change set 'never sees one set twice'. Phase 3's Verify line ('fires on a second red of one set') tests a state the lane never produces. The tripwire is one of the existing `make land` checks (D4 lists it among the first pass's checks) that FR-003 says the lane runs and FR-008 says is not dropped. This exception is plausible at the level of wording but empties the check. Required: inside the lane it must still be able to fire on repeated red on the same work, for example a repair's hand-in red again, or one task ejected twice, while staying quiet on a halving's own steps. The plan says how and tests a path that the lane can actually reach.

decisions.id: XVI-c / D3 (rebase as a no-commit apply)
decisions.summary: FR-002's 'rebases onto current main' is done as the builder's diff applied onto origin/main with carry.rs's merge rules (cherry-pick -n) and then committed, because the project forbids git rebase.
decisions.why: The request's purpose ('Conflicts and bookkeeping refusals then get fixed by the builder that has the context, in its own tree') is met in full. The work ends on current main, conflicts stop in the builder's tree for the builder to resolve, and then the first pass and the commit follow in FR-002's order. The only thing lost is the builder's intermediate commits, which nothing asks for. This is a mechanism, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: In phase 1 the hand-in applies onto the clone's HEAD rather than origin/main; from phase 2 onto origin/main.
decisions.why: In phase 1 the coordinator still lands from its clone, so the clone's HEAD is the main that the work lands on. Applying onto origin/main would put the work on a base without the staged work it was handed out on, which defeats the stated purpose of a hand-in that 'arrives on what it lands on'. From phase 2 the literal origin/main holds. This is a purpose-level justification and is temporary.

decisions.summary: The hand-in asks the first-pass checks a builder can answer and leaves writer_refusal, the mark's hold, the tripwire, claims-in-flight and the gate stamp rows to the lane, which asks them again when it lands.
decisions.why: FR-002 says 'the landing's cheap first pass'. The left-out checks either cannot be answered before a gate (the stamp rows are physically impossible), concern another writer or the ordering of other tasks, or refuse for reasons no builder can cure. Asking them in a builder's tree would defeat the sketch's purpose of having builders fix what they have the context to fix. All of them are still asked at landing, so FR-008 holds. No coverage runs, as FR-002 requires.

decisions.summary: LANE_MAX=6 and LANE_WAIT_S=0 are seeded from the two-tier ceiling and the trial's 'stronger version', because trial 458 has no finding yet; its verdict resets both.
decisions.why: FR-004 seeds the knob from trial 458's finding, and that finding does not exist yet, so seeding from it is impossible today. The GM told the session to start now. The plan labels both values GUESS and commits to resetting them from the trial's verdict.

decisions.id: D5 batch membership vs FR-003 'in order'
decisions.summary: A batch takes every waiting hand-in of the OLDEST hand-in's feature, so a later hand-in of that feature goes ahead of an earlier hand-in of another feature.
decisions.why: FR-003 says the lane 'takes hand-ins from the done refs in order', and D5 itself reads that as hand-in order ('oldest first'). The reason given, that `make land` takes one F=, does not require a reorder. A batch made of the oldest hand-in plus the CONSECUTIVE same-feature hand-ins after it keeps one F= and keeps the order. The reorder buys larger batches, which is a design preference and not one of the grounds for an exception. Required: keep hand-in order, or state the departure as an exception to FR-003 that is ruled on.

decisions.summary: Until phase 3, a red that the gate's record cannot place ejects the whole batch as one repair entry instead of halving.
decisions.why: This is rollout order, not a narrowing of the finished feature: phase 3 in this same plan replaces it with the halving and 'land the rest'. Under XV a phase-3 stall would leave it standing, so FR-004 is met only once phase 3 lands, and the feature is not done until then. Its one entry covers the whole batch, so it is also a fresh agent per batch.

decisions.id: D12 LIKE-window test omits machine load
decisions.summary: A window is LIKE when it holds 8 or more hours of builder work and its time-weighted trees held is within 0.5 of the night's; the machine's load is read but is not part of the test.
decisions.why: FR-010 defines a LIKE window as one whose 'concurrency is close ...: trees held, time-weighted ..., and the machine's load'. The load is one of the two named components, and it is the GM's seventh-message concern ('how much was happening at the time') on a shared container. D12 drops it from the likeness test without saying so, and phase 5 picks 'the first like window' by that test. A window of three trees under very different load would count as like. No justification is given, and the load median is already available (`make sampler-report`). Required: the likeness test includes a load band (a GUESS), and where load differs, both loads are stated beside the figure. Phase 5 already states each figure with its concurrency, so this finding is confined to the likeness test.

decisions.summary: The lane runs in the existing <clone>-land worktree, adopted into the pool under a reserved holder outside the cap.
decisions.why: The spec leaves the tree to the plan. FR-003's 'its own worktree' is met.

decisions.summary: The lane is a detached `l7r-gate lane --work` runner under flock, using the project's runner pattern; the Workflow tool and the Refinery were priced and not taken whole.
decisions.why: The sketch says 'run as a script in its own worktree rather than in my turns'. FR-009's reuse question is answered and recorded (R1).

decisions.summary: Each attempt gets its own file; attribution comes from the gate's Phase lines; halving lands as it goes and ejects the last survivor without a run of its own; there is no flake retry.
decisions.why: This is FR-004 and the sketch's 'bisects and ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands'. Nothing pushes ungated (FR-008).

decisions.summary: Repair entries live in the common git dir; the queue serves repairs first (LANE_REPAIR_FIRST).
decisions.why: The entries stay out of the coordinator's tree (FR-001), and the knob is labeled.

decisions.summary: States are computed from refs and an append-only lane log; 'carried' is read against origin/main.
decisions.why: This is internal mechanism and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The wake-up is `make lane-wait` in the background, one status line per batch; a Stop-guard rule refuses the main session's stop while lane work waits and no lane-wait runs; the prompt hook prints unread lines.
decisions.why: FR-005's wake-up. The Stop rule's reach is only what makes FR-005's wake happen, which is enforcement of the request.

decisions.id: D10 guard fixture, T405 option C
decisions.summary: FR-001 holds because gates run only in the lane tree, pinned by a fixture over two trees; T405 closes by its option (C).
decisions.why: This enforces FR-001.

decisions.summary: After a like window of lane landings, `make land` outside the lane tree is refused (LAND_HERE_OK escape) and land-alone steps 1-6 retire; step 7 moves to take-tip.sh; writers.rs stays.
decisions.why: The refusal enforces FR-001 and makes the lane the one route. Keeping writers.rs honors FR-008.

decisions.summary: One measurement script over both windows: tokens by actor as window totals, task size beside each figure, concurrency stated with each figure, the before figure taken in phase 0.
decisions.why: This is FR-006, FR-007 and FR-010 apart from the likeness test ruled above. Fresh integration agents are left out of the actor list because D7 makes them repair builders, and FR-006 still counts them.

decisions.id: D13 handout refused on unpushed clone commits
decisions.summary: A handout is refused while the clone holds commits that origin/main lacks; the coordinator pushes spec-only filings DIRECT.
decisions.why: This is required by D3's base, and it honors US1's 'nothing it writes waits on a gate' with the existing DIRECT route. The moved coverage premise is measured, not built around.

decisions.summary: A successor or repair handout applies the earlier done commit uncommitted and supersedes its ref; it waits only on an open batch.
decisions.why: Internal mechanism that serves the sketch.

decisions.summary: One new crate; phases 0-5; the knob table.
decisions.why: No decision here narrows the request.

decisions.summary: Only fix and closing-half builders run make builder-done; build halves and measurements keep 'Do NOT stage, commit, land or push' and the session hands them in as before; the gap is filed as T44, landing before T10.
decisions.why: The approved sketch (item 2) and US2 say builders hand in their own work, and this task leaves two kinds of task out. The literal rule cannot be met for those kinds right now. The hand-in's first pass runs the tick check's approach_refusal, which refuses a stub Approach block. A build half always has one and a measurement writes no plan section, so their hand-in is refused whoever runs it, and a builder told to run it would only get the refusal. The carve-out does not defeat the request's purpose of having refusals met by the builder with the context. It is temporary and tracked: T44 is filed in this feature and must land before T10, so the known defect is fixed before the next step and is not carried past it. The block's own label of 'easier' is not what justifies it. The impossibility does.

decisions.id: T43-D2 the block's new HAND IN line and last line
decisions.summary: fix and closing-half blocks gain the make builder-done line (conflict resolved in the tree, refusal answered and rerun, outcome and done ref reported); the last line becomes 'Commit only by make builder-done; never land or push; never rewrite history.'; the other lines are kept within the 2,000-character cap.
decisions.why: This is US2 and FR-002 as written: builders hand in once ready and fix conflicts and refusals in their own tree. Landing and pushing stay with the lane and session (FR-003), and the brief's other rules are kept.

decisions.id: T43-D3 a claims refusal reported verbatim, not answered
decisions.summary: The builder answers a refusal and reruns, except a claims refusal, which it reports verbatim.
decisions.why: The sketch hands 'conflicts and bookkeeping refusals' to the builder. A claims refusal is neither, and the brief's existing claims exit is kept rather than changed. Nothing that was asked is withheld.

decisions.id: T43-D4 builder-done added to the wrap-up band; a conflict past the cap goes to the handoff
decisions.summary: The context-cap band lets a builder past 300k run make builder-done. A conflict there needs an edit the band refuses, so it goes to the handoff.
decisions.why: This enforces the requested hand-in for a capped builder (the probe found the band refusing it). Keeping the band's existing refusal of edits only preserves behavior the GM did not ask to change.

decisions.id: T43-D5 the one git add a pool tree allows
decisions.summary: Builders may git add only a hand-in conflict's paths.
decisions.why: Without it the builder cannot resolve its own conflicts (US2). The allowance is limited to that case.

decisions.summary: builder-brief.md gains THE BUILDER HANDS IN ITSELF; the report's STATE carries the hand-in outcome and COMMIT the next-dispatch line; builder_done.rs step 6 and the efficiency-tooling row say who runs it.
decisions.why: These document the requested behavior and fix a stale row. No new scope.

decisions.id: T43-D7 no coverage at hand-in; coverage stays the gate's at landing
decisions.summary: The exits run the crates' tests and make builder-checks. Coverage runs at the landing.
decisions.why: FR-002 says so verbatim, following the struck 'coverage for its own crates'.
